chapters.title: Getting started
steps: a1
Welcome to Burghood. The first time you open the app, tap Get started, then choose your month and year of birth, and tap Continue.
a2
Along the bottom are the five main sections: Map, Society, Report, Activity, and Profile.
a3
To join your community and follow your reports, sign in from Profile with Google, Apple, or your email address.

chapters.title: The community map
steps: b1
The map shows the problems your neighbors have reported, from potholes to broken streetlights. Use the chips to filter by type, or switch to a list.
b2
Open a report to see its photo, how serious it is, and who it was sent to. If it affects you too, tap Me too.

chapters.title: Reporting a problem
steps: c1
To report something, tap Report, and choose On the street.
c2
First, confirm that no one is in danger. If someone could get hurt, Burghood points you to 911. Then add a photo of the problem.
c3
Set the exact location, choose what it is and how serious it is, and add a short note.
c4
Burghood shows you who actually fixes it, with their contact details. Tap Submit report.
c5
You can follow your report in Activity, and you'll get updates as it moves along. Once it's repaired, open it and tap Mark fixed.

chapters.title: Your society
steps: d1
Society is your community's home. Tap its name to switch if you belong to more than one.
d2
Channels are group conversations for the whole community. Open one to react, reply, and post your own message.
d3
Notices are official announcements from your admins, and Docs keeps your bylaws, budgets and minutes.
d4
Admins approve new neighbors under Manage, and can share an invite code so others join straight away.

chapters.title: Finding a provider
steps: e1
In Services, just describe what you need. Type kitchen tap leaking, and Burghood finds plumbers near you.
e2
Providers your community recommends come first, background checks are badged, and sponsored listings are clearly marked.
e3
Open a profile to read reviews from real jobs, then tap Request this provider, describe the job, and add a photo.

chapters.title: For service providers
steps: f1
Providers see new work under Activity, in Jobs. They accept the job, start it, and mark it done with a note and photos.
f2
Anyone can offer their services from Profile, under For service providers. Once the Burghood team approves them, the listing fee and how to pay appear right here.

chapters.title: Closing the loop
steps: g1
Back as a resident, open the request, confirm the work is done, and leave a rating for your neighbors.
g2
Profile also has your theme, text size and notification settings. That's Burghood: fix your street, look after your home, and know your neighbors.
